input_signals.name: AccrualsWithoutPayoutDiscipline
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dvc, prstkc), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Payouts are a costly, cash-verified signal of earnings quality; high-accrual firms that also distribute little or nothing via dividends and repurchases have unverified earnings and no disciplining cash constraint, whereas high-accrual firms returning cash are far less likely to be managing earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: This flips the financing theme from capital-raising to capital-returning, testing whether payout discipline neutralises the accrual anomaly rather than whether issuance amplifies it — a substantively different mechanism from the issuance-based signals above. The rank product makes the signal maximal for low-payout, high-accrual firms and minimal for cash-distributing conservative accruers.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( add( dvc, prstkc ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ConjunctiveAccrualCashIssuance
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), ADD(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp)), at)), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The overvaluation state requires a logical conjunction: full balance-sheet operating accruals must be aggressive *and* the firm must be a genuine net taker of outside cash from both equity and debt markets; firms satisfying only one condition should not be shorted.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg now uses cash-flow-statement issuance and retirement dollars (sstk − prstkc and dltis − dltr scaled by assets) instead of csho growth, eliminating contamination from stock splits and non-cash stock-financed acquisitions that the critic flagged, while keeping the distinctive MIN-as-AND design. Both legs are continuous and asset-scaled, so quantile breakpoints remain well populated and the short leg is a clean intersection of poor accounting quality with real external cash intake.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), add( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), add( delta( dlc, 1 ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), dp ) ), at ) ), rank( sumrank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualsWithShortMaturityDebtReliance
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(dlc, ADD(dlc, dltt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt *maturity structure*, not debt issuance volume, is the binding balance-sheet pressure: firms that fund working-capital accruals while depending on short-term debt must roll that debt before the accruals convert to cash, so accrual reversals coincide with refinancing risk and force asset sales or write-downs.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a genuinely new financing channel — the archive has tested issuance flows, payout, and financing volatility, but never the maturity composition of the claims that fund the accruals. It also uses only balance-sheet items, so coverage and sample length are much better than the cash-flow-statement designs, letting us judge whether the weak gen-0 t-stats were partly a small-sample artifact.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( wcap, 1 ), dp ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( dlc, add( dlc, dltt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualOpacityFinancingDependence
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(ABS(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)), 1), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), ADD(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), dvc)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The relevant accounting attribute here is opacity rather than direction: large accruals of *either* sign make reported earnings a noisy signal of cash generation, and information risk is only priced when the firm must repeatedly convince outside capital providers, i.e. when it depends on external funding.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the economic channel from over-optimistic reporting to information risk under external-capital dependence, so it is not a directional accruals anomaly and can be non-zero for firms with large income-decreasing accruals that the archive's signed designs place in the long leg. Paired with Signal 1 it holds the financing leg fixed and varies only the accounting construct, so the two jointly identify whether the interaction runs through accrual direction or accrual magnitude.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( abs( ratio( sub( delta( wcap, 1 ), dp ), at ) ), 1 ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), add( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), ib ), dvc ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtFinancedPayoutShortfall
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A distribution that operating cash flow cannot cover, plugged with new borrowing, is the sharpest form of balance-sheet pressure: management is defending a payout signal with creditors' money while reported earnings rest on accruals, and such firms subsequently underperform as the payout or the leverage must be corrected.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the "payout verifies earnings" moderator that the archive already probed and tests the opposite state — payout in *excess* of cash generation — with both legs continuous, so there is no tie mass at zero payout in the carrier and no reliance on the ranked payout distribution the critic objected to. The mechanism is a cash-coverage gap interacted with the debt raised to fill it, which no prior archive signal expresses.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( dvt, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: PayoutDeficitEquityFunded
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), dvc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The source of the plug financing matters: covering a payout shortfall by issuing equity dilutes shareholders and signals that management prefers selling shares to cutting the distribution, which should be at least as bad as debt funding if the story is overvaluation, but weaker if the story is leverage-driven balance-sheet pressure.
input_signals.reasoning: Holding the winning carrier fixed and swapping the debt weight for clean-surplus net equity issuance makes this a decisive discriminating test between the overvaluation interpretation and the leverage-pressure interpretation of the archive's best result. The clean-surplus construction (Δceq − ib + dvc) avoids split-contaminated csho and keeps coverage comparable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( dvt, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( add( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), ib ), dvc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: BorrowToHoardWithAccrualEarnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(MIN(DELTA(che, 1), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What the borrowed money is used for identifies the problem: firms that raise debt and simply park it in cash while reporting earnings well above operating cash flow are buying liquidity insurance against an anticipated cash shortfall, and this precautionary borrowing plus weak earnings quality predicts underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN of the cash build and the debt build is a genuine use-of-funds construct — it is large only when both the cash increase and the borrowing are large, so it identifies debt-financed hoarding rather than either operating cash accumulation or debt-financed investment. This is a use-of-proceeds mechanism absent from the archive, and it is orthogonal to the payout-defence channel that currently works, so a negative result here would sharpen the interpretation of the winner rather than merely duplicate it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( min( delta( che, 1 ), delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ErodingCashGenerationDebtPlug
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)), 1), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The informative state is a multi-year erosion of cash-generating ability that management is offsetting with fresh borrowing: reported earnings can be held up by accruals while the operating cash-flow-to-assets trend slides, and firms in this slow-motion deterioration are systematically over-priced because the income statement conceals the trend.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces horizon-smoothing of a level shortfall with a genuinely different state variable — the five-year slope of cash generation, which measures deterioration rather than a one-period gap — and pairs it with contemporaneous borrowing to capture the plug. It also revisits the archive's one lesson about changes (gen-0 DELTA-based accrual legs flipped sign) with the diagnosis that a single-year accrual-gap change is noise-dominated, whereas a five-year cash-generation trend is a persistent state; a correct negative result here would show the earlier failure was measurement, not economics.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( neg( trend( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ), 1 ), rank( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DividendHikeFundedByNewDebt
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(MIN(DELTA(dvt, 1), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Escalating a payout commitment while borrowing is worse than merely maintaining one: a dividend increase funded by new debt raises fixed claims on both sides of the capital structure at once, and doing so while operating cash flow already falls short is a commitment the firm is unlikely to sustain.
input_signals.reasoning: The weight requires a simultaneous dividend increase and debt increase (MIN of the two changes), so it isolates the act of escalating commitments rather than the level of borrowing that the winner already captures — a flow-of-commitments mechanism distinct from level-of-deficit. If the alpha strengthens relative to the winner, management's forward commitment, not the current gap, is the priced information.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( dvt, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( min( delta( dvt, 1 ), delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: MaturitiesAndDividendsMetWithEquity
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, dltr), oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: When operating cash flow cannot cover the year's hard cash claims — scheduled debt retirement plus dividends — and the gap is met by selling shares, creditors and dividend recipients are effectively being paid with new shareholders' money, a state of financing stress and dilution that predicts underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing gross debt issuance with equity issuance in the weight removes the mechanical collinearity the critic identified (issuers of debt are near-definitionally its retirers), so the product can no longer proxy for debt turnover or size and instead isolates the cross-market plug: debt obligations settled from the equity market. The carrier retains the hard-obligation content (dltr) that the archive has never tested, and both legs remain oancf-anchored and asset-scaled, so coverage matches the winning family.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( add( dvt, dltr ), oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: NearTermMaturitiesUncoveredEquityPlug
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters is the obligation the firm is *about* to face rather than the one it just settled: debt in current liabilities is next year's contractual maturity, and a firm whose operating cash flow cannot cover it and which is already tapping the equity market is pre-funding a refinancing it cannot service internally.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the realized cash-flow-statement retirement with the forward-looking balance-sheet maturity stock, which is both economically prospective and far better populated, so it tests the mechanism's timing while relieving the cash-flow-statement scarcity that has held coverage near 0.085 throughout the archive. If the prospective version dominates the realized one, the effect is anticipatory refinancing stress rather than a mechanical settlement flow.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: EquityChosenOverDebtToCloseGap
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, dltr), oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, ADD(sstk, dltis))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The instrument choice, not the quantity, is the signal: a firm closing an obligation gap by tilting its gross issuance toward equity rather than debt is either shut out of credit markets or exploiting a rich share price, both of which imply low subsequent returns under pecking-order logic.
input_signals.reasoning: Holding the archive leader's carrier fixed and replacing the *amount* of equity raised with the *equity share of gross issuance* separates adverse selection and market timing from simple financing volume, which the current weight cannot distinguish. The weight is bounded in [0,1] by construction, so it preserves monotonicity in the carrier, and its only coverage cost is firms with no gross issuance at all.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( add( dvt, dltr ), oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, add( sstk, dltis ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LeveragedBuybackWithAccrualEarnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(MIN(prstkc, DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Borrowing to repurchase stock while reported earnings run ahead of operating cash flow is per-share engineering rather than value creation: leverage is added and shares retired to support EPS that the cash flow statement does not corroborate, and such firms subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN of repurchases and the debt increase identifies debt-financed buybacks specifically — neither cash-funded repurchases nor investment-driven borrowing triggers it — which is a use-of-proceeds channel the archive has only tested in its hoarding form. It also re-tests whether the accrual gap can carry a portfolio alpha when paired with a *discretionary* financing action rather than an obligation, complementing the obligation-gap family rather than duplicating it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( min( prstkc, delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: BurningAWarChestRaisedEarlier
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvt, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that consume cash while having financed themselves through several years of share sales are spending capital raised at earlier, richer valuations; the serial dependence on the equity market — not the size of the current cash pile — is what identifies the overvalued cash-burner.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the cash-stock moderator with three-year cumulative equity issuance implements the war-chest story with a financing variable rather than a liquidity variable, so it neither mechanically inverts the archived cash-buffer signal nor takes a stand against the documented cash-holdings premium. It also tests a genuinely new dimension of the winning family — repeated versus contemporaneous market dependence — which no archive signal addresses.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( dvt, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( ts_sum( sstk, 3 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ObligationCoverageRatioEquityPlug
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(oancf, ADD(ADD(dvt, dltr), dlc))), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Credit analysts judge stress by a coverage *ratio* — cash flow relative to the claims it must service — not by a difference scaled by assets; firms whose operating cash flow covers only a small fraction of dividends, maturing debt and current debt, and which are selling equity, are the ones the market misprices.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the working-capital plug moderator that fought a known anomaly and instead tests the functional form of the leading mechanism: coverage as a ratio of cash flow to total near-term claims, which is scale-free in the obligation rather than in assets and therefore ranks a small-cash-flow firm with a large maturity wall as extreme even when both are small relative to assets. Because the denominator is a sum of near-term claims that is positive for the vast majority of firms, the ratio is well behaved, and winsorization plus the bounded equity-plug weight keeps the tails and monotonicity intact.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( neg( ratio( oancf, add( add( dvt, dltr ), dlc ) ) ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DepreciationStretchingWithEquityPlug
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Lengthening depreciation schedules is the quietest way to inflate earnings — depreciation falls below the firm's own historical norm without any change in the asset base — and firms doing this while selling equity are dressing up earnings precisely when they need outside capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Depreciation policy is the one accounting-quality dimension the archive has never tested, and measuring it against the firm's own five-year norm rather than the cross-section avoids the capital-intensity confound that plagues raw dp/at comparisons. Pairing it with the equity-plug weight that the evidence shows transmits into FF5 alphas gives the new channel its best chance, and a null result would confirm that the mechanism is about cash obligations rather than reported-earnings cosmetics.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: GapWithRolloverConcentration
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, dltr), oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(dlc, ADD(dlc, dltt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The amplifier of an uncovered obligation need not be an observed financing action: a firm whose debt is concentrated in the current maturity bucket must refinance imminently, so the same gap is far more threatening when the debt structure offers no time, regardless of whether equity has yet been issued.
input_signals.reasoning: This pairs the archive's best carrier with the maturity-structure weight that once produced a strong slope on the wrong (balance-sheet accrual) carrier (fmb −2.46, alpha +0.007), so it is a clean test of whether that earlier failure was a carrier problem rather than a weight problem. Economically it distinguishes anticipated refinancing pressure from realized market dependence, and it avoids conditioning on an equity issuance that mechanically selects small growth firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( add( dvt, dltr ), oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( dlc, add( dlc, dltt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ObligationGapUnderDividendRigidity
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, dltr), oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(TS_MIN(dvt, 5), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: An uncovered obligation is only forced onto capital markets when the payout cannot be cut; a firm that has paid a dividend in every one of the last five years has established a commitment it will defend, so the rigidity of that commitment — not the current-year amount — is what converts a cash gap into dilution or leverage.
input_signals.reasoning: TS_MIN(dvt, 5) is positive only for firms with an unbroken five-year payout record and scales with the smallest dividend they were willing to sustain, making it a rigidity measure rather than a level or a re-scaling of any weight already tested. It also tilts the extreme buckets toward established payers rather than micro-cap issuers, which should stabilise portfolio composition and address the concern that the family's alphas rest on fragile small-firm tails.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( add( dvt, dltr ), oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( ts_min( dvt, 5 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: TwoSidedGapAndCapitalFlowDirection
input_signals.expression: SUB(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, dltr), oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at))), MUL(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, dltr), oancf), at)), 1), RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The short and long legs should be symmetric economic states: firms with obligations exceeding operating cash flow that issue equity are over-valued and pressured, while firms generating cash well in excess of their obligations that use it to retire shares are the disciplined opposite, and pricing both explicitly should widen the abnormal spread.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal in this family has an economically ambiguous long leg — a low value can mean a covered obligation, no equity issuance, or both — and this construction fixes that by subtracting a second, oppositely signed interaction so the bottom of the sort is populated specifically by cash-surplus repurchasers. This is a structural change in how the interaction is assembled, not another moderator, and it directly targets the diagnosed reason the family's alpha t-stats have stalled near −3.4.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( mul( winsor( ratio( sub( add( dvt, dltr ), oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) ), mul( winsor( neg( ratio( sub( add( dvt, dltr ), oancf ), at ) ), 1 ), rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DilutionSeverityOfTheObligationGap
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, dltr), oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, ceq)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Dilution matters to incumbent shareholders in proportion to the existing equity base, not to assets: selling shares worth a quarter of book equity to cover obligations is a severe transfer, and the same dollar issuance is far more damaging for a thin-equity, highly levered firm than for an equity-financed one.
input_signals.reasoning: Scaling issuance by book equity rather than assets changes which firms occupy the extreme buckets — levered, small-equity issuers replace large-asset issuers — so this is a different economic population, not an arithmetic rescaling, and it embeds the capital-structure amplification that the archive's separate leverage weights failed to deliver on the wrong carrier. It keeps the strongest available carrier so any change in evidence is attributable to the dilution-severity measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( add( dvt, dltr ), oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, ceq ) ) )

input_signals.name: StretchedDepreciationWithTotalExternalFunding
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), 1), RANK(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), ADD(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), dvc)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: If understated depreciation is penalised because it supports outside capital raising, the penalty should attach to external funding generally — debt as well as equity — rather than to share sales specifically.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing gross share sales with balance-sheet total external funding tests whether the equity market is essential to the depreciation channel, and because every input is balance-sheet or income-statement based it should push coverage above the 0.126 already achieved, which is the one dimension where this family can still gain statistical power. A weaker result would establish equity specificity; a stronger one would give the best-covered specification in the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ), rank( ratio( add( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), add( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), ib ), dvc ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: EquityChurnWithAccrualEarnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(MIN(sstk, prstkc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that issue and repurchase equity simultaneously are running compensation-driven dilution offset by buybacks; the repurchase disguises the dilution and supports per-share metrics, and when reported earnings are not cash-backed this churn marks managed reporting rather than shareholder returns.
input_signals.reasoning: MIN(sstk, prstkc) is positive only when both flows are large, isolating churn from either genuine capital raising or genuine capital return — a financing state no archive signal has tested and one that neutralises the known positive-return repurchase effect by requiring offsetting issuance. Pairing it with the cash-flow accrual gap keeps the carrier in the measurement basis that has consistently transmitted to FF5 alphas.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( min( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DividendAffordableOnlyViaUnderDepreciation
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(MUL(at, MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5)), dp), dvt), at), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accounting policy, payout capacity and external funding form a triangle: the dollar shortfall of depreciation versus the firm's own five-year norm measures earnings manufactured by policy, and when that shortfall is as large as the dividend being paid, the distribution is affordable only because the charge was understated — a firm in that state selling equity is funding the payout from shareholders while reporting policy-inflated profits.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the rediscovery-prone asset-growth composite with a construct that has no published counterpart: MIN(depreciation shortfall, dividend) is positive only when both a policy shortfall and a real cash distribution exist, so it cannot be reproduced by asset growth or issuance sorts. It keeps the equity-plug weight whose transmission to FF5 alphas is established, and its economics tie the archive's two most successful carriers — payout commitment and depreciation policy — into a single quantity rather than an ensemble.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( min( sub( mul( at, ma( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ), dp ), dvt ), at ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DecliningDepreciationRateTrendWithDilution
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)), 1), RANK(RATIO(sstk, ceq)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A sustained multi-year decline in the depreciation rate is a policy choice rather than a one-year fluctuation — asset lives are being lengthened or costs capitalised year after year — and firms following that policy while selling equity large relative to their book equity are inflating the earnings on which incumbent shareholders are being diluted.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the single-year deviation-from-norm with the five-year slope changes the economic object from a transitory accrual deviation to a persistent accounting-policy drift, which is both less noisy and less mechanically tied to one year's asset-base jump — the confound the critic raised about the deviation carrier. Pairing it with the dilution-severity weight is justified by that weight's best-in-archive slope (fmb −3.60), and because the carrier is now a trend rather than a deviation the pair is not a rescaling of the existing dp-stretching signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( neg( trend( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ), 1 ), rank( ratio( sstk, ceq ) ) )

input_signals.name: DepreciationDeviationWithPayAndRaiseState
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), 1), RANK(RATIO(MIN(dvt, sstk), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The dividend can enter this mechanism either as the quantity that the manufactured earnings finance or as evidence of a contradictory policy — paying shareholders while simultaneously selling them shares — and the second channel implies the deviation should be modulated by the pay-and-raise state rather than truncated by the dividend.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the structural alternative to the leader: the dividend moves from the carrier's truncation into the weight, where MIN(dvt, sstk) fires only for firms doing both things at once, so comparing the two tells us whether the leader's strength comes from measuring manufactured earnings *in dollars of commitment* or from selecting contradictory financing behaviour.
